title: Two processes exchanging one message
request:
a send on `a`, a message stamped 7 delivered to `b`, and both clocks read back

./your_program.sh lamport
send a
recv b 7
get b
get a
note: The trap is the +1. `b` had never ticked, so the merge alone would leave it at 7 — the same instant as the send it is supposed to follow. The extra tick is what makes the receive strictly later than the send, and `get` must not add another.

title: A message that arrives from the past
request:
a clock pushed to 3, then a message stamped 1 delivered to it

./your_program.sh lamport
local a
local a
local a
recv a 1
get a
note: A Lamport clock is monotonic per process, so an old message can never pull one back. Writing `ts + 1` instead of `max(local, ts) + 1` passes every test where messages happen to arrive in order and fails the moment one is late.
